result.title: Is Your Long-Horizon Benchmark Really Deep? Measuring and Synthesizing Depth in Terminal Tasks
result.summary: Long-horizon terminal tasks are used to evaluate and train agents. Human-curated datasets are scarce, so many synthesis methods have emerged. They usually measure the length of a task by the turns a model needs to pass it, and its difficulty by labels the LLM sets during generation. We find, however, that the turn count largely reflects the habits of the model, not only the demands of the task, and that the labels barely track how often models pass. We describe a terminal task by its work, the number of operations it requires, and its depth, the number of turns that must happen in sequence because the commands of each turn can only be chosen after reading the output of the previous one. Estimating depth as the smallest turn cap, stated to the agent, under which the task passes, we audit 734 tasks from six existing datasets. Synthesis has mostly added work, not depth: 94% of the solved synthetic tasks pass within three turns, yet depth, unlike the turn count, predicts difficulty beyond work. We propose DEPTH, in which a generation agent writes each task one segment at a time in a real software environment, carrying out each segment before writing it and starting the next from the state it leaves. Our 105 tasks exceed every audited dataset in depth and work, and none of six current models passes half of them. Fine-tuning Qwen3-8B on runs from these tasks improves it on two terminal benchmarks.

AI.brief_summary: 该文审计六个数据集的 734 个终端任务，指出轮数更多反映模型习惯而非任务需求，提出以「最小可通过轮数上限」估计任务深度，并构建 DEPTH 分段生成更深的 105 个任务，微调 Qwen3-8B 后在两个终端基准上提升。
AI.relevance_reason: 其区分「工作量」与「须依序读取输出才能决策的深度」，并发现深度比轮数更能预测难度，可能为 LVR 的动态计算、停止决策与轨迹监督提供任务构造和评测线索，可供核查其向多模态推理的迁移。
